How the forecast works

Daily scale readings naturally move with hydration, food, sodium, and timing. Line emphasizes a 7-day moving average, then fits a simple linear trend to up to 42 recent days. Predictions extend that observed trend; they are estimates, not promises.

The confidence label uses the amount of data, time covered, and how closely readings follow the trend. A changing routine, medication, illness, or water balance can make the forecast wrong.

For intentional weight loss, the CDC describes about 1–2 lb per week as gradual and more likely to be maintained. NHLBI notes that losing 3–5% of current weight can improve some health measures. Goals are personal—consider a clinician if you are pregnant, under 18, have an eating-disorder history, or have a condition or medicine that affects weight.
